problemStatement: Links need an optional expiry after which they stop redirecting and answer 410 Gone, and deleting a link must stop it redirecting at once: today a deleted link keeps redirecting from the cache for up to 24 hours (known issue BF-1).

functional.text: POST /api/v1/links accepts an optional expiresAt (ISO-8601 instant) or an optional ttlSeconds (integer seconds from now), not both; the created link's expiry is returned as expiresAt.
An unusable expiry is rejected with 400 and type /problems/invalid-expiry: both fields given, ttlSeconds outside 1-315360000, or expiresAt not in the future or more than ten years ahead.
GET /{code} of a link whose expiry has passed returns 410 Gone with type /problems/link-expired, whether the answer comes from a cache level or the database.
Deleting a link stops it redirecting at once: the next GET /{code} returns 404 link-not-found even if the link was cached (fixes BF-1).
GET /api/v1/links/{code} shows expiresAt (absent when the link never expires).

nonFunctional.text: No cache level serves a link after its expiry, and the Redis entry of an expiring link lives no longer than the time left before expiry.
Links that never expire behave exactly as before, including their Redis entries, so old and new instances can run side by side during a rolling deploy.
The redirect path adds no database read for cached links: the expiry check uses the cached entry.

acceptanceCriteria.when: a link is created with ttlSeconds 3600
a link is created with expiresAt 2030-06-01T12:00:00Z
it has both fields, ttlSeconds 0 or 315360001, or expiresAt now, in the past or 11 years ahead

acceptanceCriteria.given: a link with ttlSeconds 60 that has redirected once
acceptanceCriteria.then: 410 with type /problems/link-expired, from L1, from Redis and from the database

acceptanceCriteria.given: a link that has redirected once (cached)

acceptanceCriteria.then: its Redis key's TTL is at most 600 seconds
its Redis value is U:<url> as before, and it still redirects ten years later

assumptions: Expiry is fixed at creation; changing it later is out of scope.
An expired link keeps status ACTIVE in the database: expiry is a time, not a status, so nothing needs to run when a link expires.
Deletion invalidates this instance's L1 and the shared Redis entry; other instances' in-process L1 entries can live until shortener.cache.l1-ttl (5 minutes).

ambiguities.question: Should an expired link answer 410 Gone or 404 like a deleted one?
Must deletion also clear other instances' in-process caches at once?
options: yes, with a Redis pub/sub broadcast
no, they expire within the L1 TTL
ambiguities.proposedDefault: no: bounded by the 5-minute L1 TTL; noted as a follow-up

outOfScope: Changing or removing an expiry after creation
Purging expired links from the database
